2 months back, i took a ride from Bellandur to Kalyan Nagar and back( I live in Bangalore ) with the specific intention of taking pictures along the outer ring road to capture the negligence of the authorities who are in charge of cleaning the roads in this stretch. The mud and sand are neatly arranged as small mountains( kids might love to see them !! ) on the footpath. Again they exist till date!! 3) The state of underpasses at the center of the underpass right under the bridge on top, should be seen, mainly the Ram Murthy Nagar and Horamavu underpass. When someone has swept the road, am sure some money would have paid for doing the same, why is the stuff not being picked up!! Instead it is left lying there, in fact you can see plants growing in many of these sand/mud mounds!! Can't Bangalore have cleaner roads, is it that difficult? Many a times citizens add to the mess by throwing garbage on top of these mounds of sand/mud. Please stop doing this!! I have not seen this state in any other city. The idea of taking the pics was that reaches the concerned authorities and they take some action. Now, just uploading the photos( around 50 of them ) would have been very boring. I've lived in several areas of Bangalore, including Indiranagar, Whitefield, and Kammanahalli, and my particular area of RT Nagar is the most unnecessarily noise-polluted part of Bangalore I've encountered. The cause is cart-pushing vendors who use loudspeakers, and these are usually recordings that are on an endless loop. When I moved here two years ago, there were two or three vendors who used loudspeakers; currently, they number about 20. Two important points: 1) I am not opposed to cart vendors making a living in this or any other area; most of them simply use their natural voice to call out once every 10 or 20 meters. That's fine. Loudspeakers--particularly those with recordings on an endless loop--are unnecessary noise pollution that are a complete lack of consideration for the neighborhood. Many of us have to work online, conducting meetings and teaching classes, and banana salesmen using loudspeaker recordings should not have priority over the tasks of others who must work at home. 2) My understanding is that these loudspeakers are already illegal in Bangalore, as I've read that any kind of public address system in this city must be at a volume that cannot be audible for more than 200 meters. I would like to see this law enforced, as this area is suffering from a great deal of unnecessary noise pollution that is impeding the productivity and peace of mind of those of us who work at home and those who simply want to enjoy a day of quietude. In addition to the illegality and rudeness of these loudspeakers, I'll conclude by observing that many of these endless-loop recordings in my area are absolutely ABSURD in regard to the way they sound: It's as though the vendors deliberately created recordings that sound ridiculous, obnoxious, and agitating...and inexplicably believing such would attract a happy clientele.
